tasks.q: Which pair needs swapping for ascending order?
Order the states in the first left-to-right pass.
tasks.fb: The largest item moves right one comparison at a time.

tasks.q: After the first pass on [5,1,4,2], the final item is...
tasks.fb: 5. Work from left to right in these examples.

tasks.q: After pass 1 gives [2, 3, 1, 4], what does pass 2 give?
After two passes on [5,1,4,2], the list is...
tasks.fb: 1,2,4,5. A pass does not always finish the sort.

tasks.q: First full pass on [1, 2, 3, 4]: how many swaps?
A comparison always produces a swap. Is this true?
tasks.fb: No. A comparison may not cause a swap.
Both original values must survive the swap.

tasks.q: Without saving a value before overwriting it, a swap may...
tasks.fb: Lose an original value. Keep one value temporarily.

tasks.q: Which is a safe early stopping condition?
a: A complete pass makes no swaps
The list contains an even number
tasks.fb: A complete pass makes no swaps

tasks.q: When should swapped be reset to false?
tasks.fb: Before each pass. Track whether any swap occurred.

tasks.q: First full left-to-right bubble pass on [4, 3, 2, 1] gives...
Why can the rightmost value then be excluded?
a: It is the largest and is in its final position
All other values are now sorted
tasks.fb: It is the largest and is in its final position

info.title: Compare neighbours
info.text:
Compare adjacent values.

Swap if the left value is greater.

Leave correctly ordered neighbours unchanged.

Challenge: Should equal neighbouring values be swapped?

No. They are already in a valid ascending order.

info.title: Complete the first pass
info.text:
Work from left to right in these examples.

Compare each adjacent pair in turn.

The largest value reaches the right-hand end.

Challenge: Is the list fully sorted after this pass?

No. 4 and 2 are still out of order, though 5 is in its final position.

info.title: Continue the passes
info.text:
A pass does not always finish the sort.

The next pass fixes the next-largest value.

An optimised version excludes the sorted end.

Challenge: What is the list after the second pass?

1, 2, 4, 5.

info.title: Swaps and comparisons
info.text:
A comparison may not cause a swap.

Keep comparison and swap counts separate.

A full first pass on four items compares three pairs.

Challenge: How many comparisons and swaps occur?

Three adjacent comparisons and one swap.

info.title: Read the swap
info.text:
Keep one value temporarily.

Overwrite its original position safely.

Restore the saved value in the other position.

Challenge: Why is temp needed in this three-line swap?

It preserves the original a[i] so it is not lost when a[i] is overwritten.

info.title: Stop when unchanged
info.text:
Track whether any swap occurred.

A complete pass with no swaps shows sorted order.

Reset the swap flag before each new pass.

Challenge: Why is one correct pair not enough to stop?

Other adjacent pairs may still be out of order. The whole active pass must be checked.
